subject.title: [Feature]: Pluggable STT backend for macOS Push-to-Talk

question: Should native macOS Push-to-Talk gain a batch STT backend seam, and should the first implementation bridge to Gateway `tools.media.audio` instead of adding a separate native HTTP or command backend?
rationale: The missing capability is clear, but maintainers must choose product ownership, credential handling, private-network policy, fallback semantics, and overlay UX before a safe implementation can be scoped.

options.title: Design Gateway-backed batch PTT seam
options.body: Keep Apple Speech as the default and add a final-text batch backend that reuses existing media/provider request controls and explicit fallback policy.

options.title: Fold into broader native ASR design
options.body: Track this as the macOS PTT slice of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46661 until maintainers choose a shared native/provider contract.

options.title: Defer native backend selection
options.body: Keep native PTT on Apple Speech until a broader voice-input plan across PTT, Talk, wake-word, and mobile surfaces is ready.

recommendation.title: Design Gateway-backed batch PTT seam
recommendation.body: Keep Apple Speech as the default and add a final-text batch backend that reuses existing media/provider request controls and explicit fallback policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The first decision is the native macOS voice owner boundary, and steipete has the strongest PTT and macOS voice feature-history signal.
